issues.description: Contract violation: delimiter argument raises ValueError on bad input but signature/docstring don't declare it
issues.detail: The new precondition (delimiter must be in _PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS) is enforced by raising ValueError, but the Raises section only documents HTTPBadRequest. Callers reading the spec cannot know unsupported delimiters throw. Either document the ValueError in the Raises clause or validate at a layer that converts to HTTPBadRequest. A contract that surprises callers is a failed contract.

issues.description: LSP-adjacent inconsistency: delimiter silently no-ops when value is already a list, violating principle of least surprise
issues.detail: The postcondition of get_param_as_list with delimiter is conditional on the runtime type of params[name]. A caller passing delimiter='|' expects splitting; if upstream parsing produced a list, splitting is skipped silently. This is a weakened postcondition relative to the documented behavior. The Note documents it, but the contract would be cleaner if delimiter also re-split list elements, or explicitly rejected the combination.

issues.description: Leaky abstraction: symbolic constants and literal characters share a single namespace via dict lookup
issues.detail: _PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS conflates two different abstract types — OpenAPI symbolic style names ('pipeDelimited') and literal delimiter characters ('|'). The contract would be clearer as a typed enum or a Literal union. Today a future delimiter character collision (e.g., adding 'p' as a delimiter) would conflict with 'pipeDelimited' silently because both are string keys.

issues.description: Missing test for invariant: delimiter argument with default/missing param path
issues.detail: The contract should specify that delimiter has no effect when the param is absent (default path returns default). No test exercises get_param_as_list with delimiter set AND missing param, so the postcondition for that branch is unverified. Small test addition would lock the contract.

review.summary: The feature is well-scoped and the abstract data type — a parameter-list extractor with optional delimiter — is reasonable. The main contract weaknesses are: (1) the ValueError raised on unsupported delimiter is not declared in the Raises clause, breaking the documented interface contract; (2) the delimiter argument silently no-ops when the value is already a list, which weakens the postcondition; and (3) symbolic-name and literal-character delimiters share a single dict namespace, which would read more cleanly as a typed enum. ADT-SOUND with minor SPEC-MISSING and LEAKY-ABSTRACTION notes.
